A checkout-minted token IS a pre-signed remedy, so Lightning's ordering rule applies: **the revocation path exists before the first token is minted, or the migration to add one runs on live subscribers.** **THE INTENT-BLINDNESS CAVEAT IS THE FINDING.** A token whose second presentation is read as theft cannot tell a thief from a customer, and the honest cases are ordinary: second device, password-manager autofill, browser prefetch, **corporate mail scanners fetching the link before the human does**, forwarding the receipt to whoever handles the money, and a reload after a 500. **The harm is asymmetric in the unexpected direction:** what single-use prevents is a leaked portal; what it CAUSES is a paying customer who cannot cancel, with no login and no second route. **THE PLATFORM ALREADY SHIPPED THE RIGHT ANSWER** &mdash; `api/sen-portal.js` + `sql/sairnsenior_portal_links_schema.sql`: 256-bit token, `client_id` resolved FROM the token, `active` + `revoked_at` as the remedy, `last_accessed_at`, and deliberately NO use counter and NO expiry. Reuse is OBSERVED, never fatal. **AND ONE PROPERTY TODAY'S CODE HAS BY ACCIDENT OF SHAPE:** `sairncash.html:741-748` mints a FRESH portal session on every click, so minting on demand is intent-blind-safe by construction and a checkout-minted single-use token would be a REGRESSION on that axis. **TWO THINGS FOUND WHILE SCOPING:** `api/sairncash/portal.js` has NO rate limit and is unauthenticated (`api/_lib/anon-rate-limit.js` already exists), and there is **no `api/sairncash/portal.test.js`** &mdash; the endpoint whose whole security design is *do not trust the caller's identifier* has no arm asserting it, so a future edit accepting `req.body.customerId` would be caught by nothing | M |
